title: ThermoTargetMiner: Proteome Integral Solubility Alteration (PISA) target database for prospective lung cancer drug candidates
projectDescription: Knowledge of the targets of therapeutic compounds helps understanding the compound action mechanism as well as the side-effects. The multiple complementary techniques needed for comprehensive target characterization must combine data reliability with sufficient analysis throughput. Here, we test the Proteome Integral Solubility Alteration (PISA) assay by target identification of 67 approved anticancer drugs and candidates against pulmonary carcinoma.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Samples were prepared following our PISA protocol (DOI: 10.1007/978-1-0716-2624-5_7). A549 and H82 lysate or cells were treated with the selected anti-cancer compounds at 10 µM concentration.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw LC-MS/MS data were processed for protein identification and quantification using MaxQuant software (2.5.0.0). Data post-processing was performed in R and OPLS-DA models were built using SIMCA 17 (Sartorius).
